title: Ab Initio Approach for Quantum Magnets with Coupled Cluster and Transcorrelation
authors: Kristoffer Simula, Nikolay A. Bogdanov, Olle Gunnarsson, Daniel Kats, Ali Alavi
abstract: The nearest-neighbour exchange coupling $J_1$ is the simplest ingredient of model Hamiltonians used to understand magnetism in real materials. Nevertheless, its ab initio determination requires a high-level correlation treatment and a large basis for wave function expansion. Here we compute $J_1$ for five oxygen-bridged spin-1/2 quantum magnets --- Sr$_2$CuO$_3$, La$_2$CuO$_4$, NdNiO$_2$, ZnCu$_3$(OH)$_6$Cl$_2$, and Li$_2$CuO$_2$ --- spanning bridging angles from 180$^\circ$ to 94$^\circ$ and the crossover from antiferromagnetic to ferromagnetic coupling, using embedded-cluster methodology. To describe the open-shell singlets we use 2-determinant coupled cluster with single and double excitations, which recovers the orbital-breathing enhancement of superexchange from a minimal reference. Basis-set errors are found to be large: extrapolation to the complete basis-set (CBS) limit shifts $J_1$ by up to 50 meV from bases of double-$ζ$ quality. Transcorrelated Hamiltonians reproduce the CBS estimates with modest basis set sizes, yielding an excellent accuracy against experiment at highly affordable cost. These results are the first application of transcorrelated methods in strongly correlated solid-state systems, and establish transcorrelation as a powerful theory in computational research of materials.
summary: This work presents an advanced *ab initio* method to calculate the magnetic exchange coupling ($J_1$) in various quantum magnets. By applying transcorrelated (TC) theory, the authors overcome the severe basis set limitations of standard coupled cluster approaches. The results establish TC as a highly accurate and computationally affordable tool for studying strongly correlated materials across different magnetic regimes.
main_problem: The primary challenge is accurately determining the nearest-neighbour exchange coupling ($J_1$) in quantum magnets, a calculation that demands high-level correlation treatments and large basis sets.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that transcorrelated (TC) methods can reproduce Complete Basis Set (CBS) estimates for $J_1$ with modest basis sets, achieving high accuracy at a low computational cost.
method: The study employs embedded-cluster methodology using 2-determinant coupled cluster (2det-CC) and introduces and validates the transcorrelated (TC) approach for strongly correlated solid-state systems.
model_or_system: The calculations are performed on five oxygen-bridged spin-1/2 quantum magnets ($	ext{Sr}_2	ext{CuO}_3$, $	ext{La}_2	ext{CuO}_4$, etc.) spanning geometries that induce a crossover from antiferromagnetic to ferromagnetic coupling.
key_observables: The nearest-neighbour exchange coupling ($J_1$) and the singlet-triplet gap ($	ext{E}_{	ext{ST}}$) in model systems.
important_parameters: Bridging angles ranging from $180^\circ$ to $94^\circ$; the need to extrapolate results to the Complete Basis Set (CBS) limit.
main_assumptions: The primary approximations involve using 2-determinant coupled cluster (limited to single and double excitations) and the necessity of including 'orbital-breathing effects' to capture superexchange accurately.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the notes reference tables comparing $	ext{E}_{	ext{ST}}$ across different methods and figures illustrating the crystal structures and embedding clusters used.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the difficulty of calculating $J_1$ using standard methods, then applies 2det-CC and introduces TC theory, demonstrating its superior accuracy and efficiency compared to standard CC methods when approaching the CBS limit.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state magnetism, the development and application of transcorrelated methods represent a powerful, generalizable theoretical tool for accurately treating strong electron correlation in complex quantum systems, which has relevance across many-body physics.
